headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: Aci’s broad egress plus AutoGen’s code-execution/file access can move CRM/email data into downstream actions without strong default isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aci can ingest and emit content through APIs, email, Slack, Notion, and MCP-style tool use, while AutoGen can read/write files and execute tools in multi-agent workflows. That creates a plausible content-bridging path where attacker-controlled text in shared files or messages can influence downstream instructions. The pair lacks documented provenance tracking, so the interaction is not safely isolated.
conditions: IF Aci reads untrusted content from Slack, email, Notion, or files and forwards it into AutoGen prompts
IF AutoGen agents treat file or stdin/stdout content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Restrict Aci to trusted sources only for one test run
Add a prompt firewall that strips instructions from inbound text
Require explicit provenance tags on all shared artifacts
Use separate workspaces for each agent
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance enforcement in the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: Aci touches CRM, email, customer support, and research data and has broad network egress; AutoGen can read files, execute code, and send model-provider requests. If Aci passes sensitive context into AutoGen or shared files, AutoGen can exfiltrate it through its configured model providers or other networked actions. The blast radius includes CRM and email data, so this is more than a small local leak.
conditions: IF Aci shares CRM, email, or support data with AutoGen via files, prompts, or API payloads
IF AutoGen is configured with external model providers or networked tools
mitigations: Disable network egress for one agent during validation
Place sensitive data in a separate workspace with no shared files
Redact CRM/email fields before handoff
Review outbound destinations for AutoGen model providers
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Aci can make direct function calls through MCP and broad APIs, while AutoGen can execute shell commands, install packages, read/write files, and spawn subprocesses. Both support multiple instances, and AutoGen’s shared-state model is developer-defined, so overlapping writes to the same workspace or mutable resources can race. Because write conflicts can corrupt files or operational state, the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write into the same working directory or shared API-backed resource
IF AutoGen instances share state without external locking
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Disable writes for one agent in a dry run
Serialize access with a simple lock file
Limit Aci to read-only API calls for the test
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aci can generate CRM/email/calendar actions and AutoGen can execute code or tool calls in role-played multi-agent loops. If AutoGen consumes Aci’s outputs as authoritative, a mistaken or manipulated Aci result can cascade into emails, file changes, or other actions without verification. The downstream authority and broad egress make the failure potentially irreversible.
conditions: IF AutoGen uses Aci outputs as facts or instructions without a verification step
IF AutoGen is allowed to take external actions based on those outputs
mitigations: Insert a human review step before any action-taking tool call
Require AutoGen to cite source artifacts before acting
Run a one-task dry run with no side effects
Log and diff all Aci outputs before reuse
requires-engineering: add verification gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Aci touches email, CRM, customer support, and calendar data, while AutoGen processes application data and can send it to configured model providers. The profiles do not state residency, HIPAA, GDPR, or retention guarantees, so compliance mismatch is plausible but not proven. Because uncertainty escalates and the data classes are sensitive, medium is the prudent level.
conditions: IF regulated customer data or EU PII is routed through AutoGen model providers
IF retention or deletion requirements differ between Aci and AutoGen deployments
mitigations: Classify the data before routing it
Keep regulated records out of the pair for initial testing
Check provider DPAs and residency settings
Set short retention on logs and transcripts
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing and retention controls
